title: useInfiniteQuery: Pagination
prompt:
Build a paginated list with `useInfiniteQuery` and a `Load more` button.

**Requirements:**
1. Import `useInfiniteQuery` from `@tanstack/react-query`.
2. Define and export `type Page = { items: { id: number; title: string }[]; nextCursor: number | null }`.
3. Define and export `fetchPage({ pageParam = 0 }: { pageParam?: number }): Promise<Page>` -- calls `fetch('/api/items?cursor=<pageParam>')` and returns the JSON.
4. Export a function component `InfiniteList()`. Inside:
   - `useInfiniteQuery({ queryKey: ['items'], queryFn: fetchPage, initialPageParam: 0, getNextPageParam: (last) => last.nextCursor })`.
   - Flatten `data?.pages.flatMap(p => p.items)` for rendering.
5. Render the items as `<li>` and a `<button>Load more</button>` that calls `fetchNextPage` -- disable it when `!hasNextPage || isFetchingNextPage`.
hints: `getNextPageParam(last)` is what makes pagination work -- return `null`/`undefined` to stop.
`data.pages` is an array of pages; `flatMap` flattens them into a single render list.
Disable the button on `!hasNextPage` AND `isFetchingNextPage` so users can't double-fire.
